input.prompt:
You are an ACSL specification expert working for a Frama-C WP verification harness. Your job: add ACSL annotations to a single C file so that Frama-C WP can prove the two original `//@ assert(...)` assertions, WITHOUT changing any original C token and WITHOUT using admit/assume/axiom/`\exists`-bypassing tricks.

SOURCE FILE TO READ (only read this; do not browse other folders):
[TASK]/workspace/input/adjacent_find.c

It contains:
- typedef int value_type; typedef unsigned int size_type;
- An axiomatic block defining: predicate HasEqualNeighbors{L}(value_type* a, integer n) = \exists integer i; 0 <= i < n-1 && a[i] == a[i+1];
- A function:
  size_type adjacent_find(const value_type* a, size_type n)
  with: if (1u < n) { for (size_type i = 0u; i + 1u < n; ++i) { if (a[i] == a[i+1u]) { //@ assert HasEqualNeighbors(a, i+2); return i; } } }  then  //@ assert !HasEqualNeighbors(a, n);

The two assertions MUST remain byte-for-byte unchanged (same text, same position).

YOUR OUTPUT: Write the fully annotated C file to:
[TASK]/workspace/output/adjacent_find/adjacent_find.acsl.c

It must contain the EXACT original C content, plus added ACSL. Recommended annotations (adjust as needed after verifying):

Add a function contract before the function, e.g.:
/*@
  requires n > 0 ==> \valid_read(a + (0 .. (integer)n-1));
  assigns \nothing;
  behavior found:
    assumes \exits;
    ensures \result == \at(i,\exit) && \result + 1 < n;
  behavior notfound:
    assumes !\exits;
    ensures !HasEqualNeighbors(a, n);
*/
(Adjust names/blocks to what actually verifies; a simple contract is also fine: e.g. requires \valid_read(a+(0..n-1)); assigns \nothing; ensures \result < n || \result == <index>; but note proofs of the asserts are what matter most.)

Add a loop annotation on the `for` loop, BEFORE the `for` keyword:
  loop invariant \at(0 <= i, Here);  (or just: 0 <= i;)
  loop invariant 0 <= i;      // i non-negative
  loop invariant i + 1 <= n;  // bound while iterating  (justify with unsigned arithmetic)
  loop invariant \forall integer j; 0 <= j < i ==> a[j] != a[j+1];
  loop assigns i;
  loop variant n - i;

KEY PROOF LOGIC YOU ARE ENFORCING (make sure your invariants achieve these):
1) First assert HasEqualNeighbors(a, i+2): since a[i]==a[i+1] (entered the if), instantiate the \exists with j=i: need 0<=i, i<i+1, a[i]==a[i+1]. Guarantee the invariant/context provides i>=0 and these facts.
2) Second assert !HasEqualNeighbors(a, n): at loop exit the loop condition i+1u<n is false so i+1>=n, i.e. i>=n-1; combined with invariant \forall j; 0<=j<i ==> a[j]!=a[j+1] this covers all j in [0,n-2]. When the loop is skipped (n<=1) the range 0..n-2 is empty so the predicate is false trivially.

VERIFICATION (run these exact commands with bash, they are the toolchain; do NOT run --help, --version, pip/opam/apt installs, or browse outside the workspace):
Verify a candidate file with:
  '/Users/dijkstra/ACSL-Agent 2/acsl模块化验证/.venv/bin/python' -m engine.harness_spectool verify --file <PATH> --timeout 15 --save-stdout <PATH>.wp.txt
Read the JSON result. Iterate: edit the .acsl.c, re-verify, up to 5 rounds, until result is "Pass" with proved == total.

You may also try the spectool `inject` command, but if the spectool parser cannot find the function (it reports "function not found"), then just edit the .acsl.c file directly with a file tool — that is the accepted approach.

CHECK-ADMIT (must be clean): run
  '/Users/dijkstra/ACSL-Agent 2/acsl模块化验证/.venv/bin/python' -m engine.harness_spectool check-admit -f <PATH>
It must return ok:true with 0 illegal admits. Never add admit/assume/axiom.

Do NOT modify or delete any original `//@ assert` line or any original C token. Only insert ACSL.

WHEN DONE, respond (in your final message text) with:
1) The final full content of adjacent_find.acsl.c
2) The verify result (proved/total and result field)
3) The check-admit result
4) Which invariants/contract clauses you used and why they prove each assert.

Do not stop early: keep fixing until verify Pass AND check-admit ok:true.
